title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X is a topological space with a stratification indexed by a poset I. The strata X_i^* are pairwise disjoint and their union is X. X_i denotes the closed stratum, the closure of X_i^*. The axioms give X_i = ⋃_{i'≤i} X_{i'}^*, where ī denotes the down-set of i.

Step 1 (the top lines). Since X_j is closed and X_i is the closure of X_i^*:
- X_i ⊂ X_j ⇔ X_i^* ⊂ X_j.
- Because the strata are disjoint, this holds ⇔ every i' ≤ i with X_{i'}^* ≠ ∅ satisfies i' ≤ j.

Step 2: faithful stratifications. Call the stratification faithful ('fidèle') when all strata are non-empty. Then (92) holds: X_i ⊂ X_j ⇔ X_i^* ⊂ X_j ⇔ i ≤ j. Consequently:
- i ↦ X_i is an order-embedding of I into (P(X), ⊂).
- I can be identified with a family of subsets of X.
- A faithful stratification is then the same as a family of non-empty closed subsets ('closed strata') with these properties: locally finite; union equal to X; 'stable under intersection'; satisfying axiom Strat 3; and such that each closed stratum minus the union of its strictly smaller closed sub-strata gives back the open stratum (density axiom, 'Strat 5').
The marginal remark notes that Strat 5 is stronger than conditions expressible purely through the closed strata. In other words, the poset of strata is recovered intrinsically from X as its 'closure poset'.

Step 3: notation for subsets J ⊂ I (93).
- X_J^* = ⋃_{j∈J} X_j^*, not necessarily closed.
- X_J = ⋃_{j∈J} X_j, closed by local finiteness.
- NB: J ↦ X_J^* commutes with unions and intersections, since it is the preimage map along X → I. In particular X_J^* ∩ X_K^* = X_{J∩K}^*.
- Grothendieck wrote, then crossed out, the analogous claim X_J ∩ X_K = X_{J∩K}, which is false.

Purpose. The previous and next pages derive the dictionary between subsets of the poset and subsets of X:
- closed (down-closed) J ↔ closed X_J^*;
- open (up-closed) L ↔ open X_L^*;
- 'bande' (convex, i.e. locally closed) J ↔ locally closed X_J^*, with closure X_{J̄}^* = X_J^* ⊔ X^*_{J̄∖J}.
This is exactly the statement that X → I is continuous (and, under density and faithfulness, 'open onto its image') for the Alexandrov topology on I. It prepares the construction of tubular/conic neighbourhoods V_i of strata, whose overlaps V_i ∩ V_j are non-empty only for comparable i, j (next page). That is the combinatorics of a cover whose nerve is the order complex of chains of I, used for the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces.
errors: The phrase 'stable par l'intersection' is too strong as written. The intersection X_i ∩ X_j of two closed strata is ⋃_{k≤i,j} X_k, a union of closed strata. It is a single closed stratum (or empty) only if i and j have a meet among the indices realised. The correct condition is presumably 'the intersection of two closed strata is a union of closed strata'.
X_J = ⋃_{j∈J} X_j is closed for infinite J only thanks to local finiteness, which is added in the margin ('loc. finie'). Without it the claim fails.
The crossed-out identity X_J ∩ X_K = X_{J∩K} is indeed false: for incomparable i, j, X_i ∩ X_j can contain lower strata while {i}∩{j} = ∅. Grothendieck correctly deleted it.
The second equivalence in the top lines uses Strat-type axioms (X_j is the union of the strata X_{i''}^* with i'' ≤ j). This is implicit rather than stated on this page.

ideas.what: For a faithful (all strata non-empty) poset-stratification, X_i ⊂ X_j ⇔ i ≤ j. So the index poset embeds into P(X) and the stratification is equivalent to a family of closed strata satisfying intrinsic axioms.
ideas.modern_name: closure poset / frontier condition; stratification determined by its closed strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; Goresky–MacPherson)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces only in general terms

ideas.what: J ↦ X_J^* is a Boolean-lattice homomorphism P(I) → P(X) (preimage along X → I). Combined with the adjacent pages: closed / open / 'bande' (convex) subsets of I correspond to closed / open / locally closed unions of strata.
ideas.modern_name: stratification as a continuous map X → I for the Alexandrov topology on the poset I
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, ~2009–2017); also Treumann's exit-path work (2009) and later Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Douteau

missed.claim: In 1981–82 Grothendieck sets up stratified spaces through a full dictionary between subsets of the poset I (open, closed, convex 'bandes') and unions of strata (open, closed, locally closed). This is essentially the now-standard definition of an I-stratified space as a continuous map to I with its Alexandrov topology, popularised by Lurie decades later. The idea is elementary, so this is a priority/record point rather than a new result.
missed.quote: NB J ↦ X_J^* est compatible aux réunions et intersections, X_J^* ∩ X_K^* = X_{J∩K}^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows the poset/Alexandrov viewpoint on stratifications was already the organising framework of Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme. That programme is the one sketched in Esquisse d'un programme and is relevant to exit-path ∞-categories and stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary point-set bookkeeping for poset-stratified spaces and is folklore today. The only mild interest is that it anticipates the Alexandrov-topology formalism of modern stratified homotopy theory inside the unpublished 'déploiement' notes.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out sentence at the bottom reads more plausibly 'Nous utiliserons cette notation surtout si J est une bande. Alors on a ...', with 'bande' rather than 'section'. The word 'bande' is Grothendieck's term for convex/locally closed subsets of I on the adjacent pages.
The marginal insertion reads 'ens. de "strates fermées", de réunion X'; 'loc. finie' replaces a crossed-out 'finie', and 'non vides' is inserted above 'fermées'.

The sentence about Strat 5 is garbled in the transcription. It seems to say that Strat 5 (each closed stratum is the closure of its open part / minus its strictly smaller sub-strata) is an axiom stronger than conditions expressible purely via the closed strata. The exact wording is uncertain.
In the top line the index after ∀ is i' (corrected from a slip) and the union is over i'' ∈ j̄.
